overview: The City Council approved the first readings of ordinances concerning behavioral health, donation collection bins, and rodent control. Councilors also pressed the administration for detailed COVID-19 vaccination rollout plans and referred proposals on tenant notification and leaf blowers to subcommittees.

items.title: Behavioral Health Commission Ordinance
items.summary: Approved the first reading of an ordinance establishing a Promote, Prevent, Support Behavioral Health Commission to coordinate city health data and services.

items.title: Unattended Donation Collection Bin Ordinance
items.summary: Approved the first reading of an ordinance regulating the placement, permitting, and maintenance of unattended clothing and property donation bins.

items.title: Health and Sanitation Rodent Control Ordinance
items.summary: Approved the first reading of an ordinance strengthening pest management and rodent control standards across permitted sites, food establishments, and residential composting.

items.title: Legal Opinion on MBTA Communities Zoning Law
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting a legal opinion from the city solicitor on whether Medford's zoning complies with state multi-unit residential requirements for MBTA communities.

items.title: Condolence Resolution for Rose Mosher
items.summary: Approved a resolution offering condolences to the family of longtime resident and Victor's Deli co-founder Rose Mosher.

items.title: Closed Captioning Cost Estimate
items.summary: Approved a request for the Director of Community Media to provide a cost estimate for adding closed captioning to City Council broadcasts.

items.title: COVID-19 Vaccination Rollout and Outreach
items.summary: Approved an amended resolution requesting weekly administration updates on vaccination distribution, local dispensing sites, and direct telephone outreach to Medford senior citizens.

items.title: City Council Legal Counsel and Legal Spending Accounting
items.summary: Approved an amended resolution requesting FY22 municipal budget funds to hire dedicated City Council legal counsel, as well as an accounting of external legal costs and municipal claims settlements.

items.title: Housing Stability Notification Ordinance
items.summary: Referred to the Elderly Affairs and Housing Subcommittee a proposal requiring landlords serving eviction notices to include information on tenant rights and assistance resources.

items.title: Charter Commission Home Rule Petition Status
items.summary: Approved a request for status updates from the administration and the state legislative delegation on the council's approved home rule petition for a charter commission.

items.title: Hormel Commission Application Deadline
items.summary: Extended the application deadline for the council's Hormel Commission vacancy to February 28, 2021, and requested copies of any applications received by the administration.

items.title: Hazardous Waste Disposal Update
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting an update from the administration regarding residential hazardous waste disposal options and membership in the Lexington Consortium.

items.title: Commercial-Grade Leaf Blower Regulations
items.summary: Referred a proposed ordinance restricting commercial-grade gas leaf blowers to the Subcommittee on Environmental Affairs for study and stakeholder input.

items.title: Committee Reports and Meeting Minutes
items.summary: Accepted a Committee of the Whole report regarding utilities on Riverside Avenue, placed ordinance committee reports on file, and approved the minutes of February 2, 2021.
